title: This Arcade Takes MEMORIES, Not Coins 🕹️
premise: At a bright arcade every game costs you the memory of ever coming there, taken at the door from whoever played last, so my name is on every high score and I have never played, and my big sister brings me for her birthday to win the giant bear on the top shelf.
twist: She has brought me every Saturday for forty weeks; I win her the same bear every time and lose the afternoon at the door, while she never plays and keeps every one. The door only takes from whoever played last, so I hand her my last token and now I remember the day for both of us.
world: A sunny arcade with grape violet carpet, cyan and orange cabinets, skee-ball lanes, an air hockey table, a coin pusher, a white prize counter, a wall of plush and a back closet full of forty identical giant bears.
